check.reason: The target is the system: billing codes, facility fees and ER-style pricing. Patients are treated as the people being failed, and nothing mocks them, the reporter, or a private individual. It has no quotes, no invented figures and no death, children or violence. The tone is dry and deadpan, and the closing line about a diagnosis that appears only after discharge is a real satirical joke. It matches the real story of a simple UTI visit producing a large bill. One minor caution: 'in the thousands' is loose next to a $1,756 example, so the producer should confirm the coughs-and-congestion detail and the ER-billing framing against the linked story.

pick.title: How a simple UTI turns into a $1,756 bill
pick.headline: Urgent Care Visit Mysteriously Upgraded to Emergency Room Pricing, No Emergency Required
pick.take: Patients went in for coughs, congestion and a UTI, and came out with ER bills in the thousands. Apparently the acuity of the visit matters less than what the billing code and the sign on the door say. It is the only diagnosis in medicine that reliably appears after discharge.
